_comment: litellm.register_model payloads for ProviderSpec default/fallback ids that LiteLLM's model table should
price but does not carry (nvh/providers/registry.py registers them at catalog load, only while the id is
absent from litellm.model_cost, so LiteLLM wins the moment a release adds the row). Every payload carries
a `source`; the loader strips it before registering. tests/test_capabilities_catalog.py checks that every
spec default and fallback prices on whatever LiteLLM is installed and that every key here is a current
Deliberately absent: perplexity/preset/* (billed from usage.cost; litellm.cost_per_token must keep raising
so the catalog rates stay the fallback -- tests/test_perplexity_surface.py), the llm7 / siliconflow bare
ids (zero-cost providers on the openai/ route; registering a bare `gpt-oss` makes litellm.get_llm_provider
route it to OpenAI), and the huggingface/* ids (ProviderSpec.metered_upstream: LiteLLM bills Hugging Face
Inference Providers at $0 whatever is registered, the real rate lands on the HF account, so the rows load as
'cost unknown' rather than a known $0 -- and litellm.register_model fetches huggingface.co/<id>/config.json
for a huggingface/ id, which the catalog load must never do). Their facts are `source:`-annotated rows in

ai21_chat/jamba-large-1.7.source: litellm model_cost['jamba-large-1.7'] (ai21 key; identical in 1.99.0 and 1.106.6) re-keyed for the ai21_chat/ route the spec uses; tool calling per docs.ai21.com (Jamba 1.7 supports function calling)

ai21_chat/jamba-mini-2.source: AI21 pricing (Jamba Mini: $0.20 / $0.40 per 1M tokens, 256K context) as carried by capabilities.yaml since 0.41.1; LiteLLM has no jamba-mini-2 row (its table stops at jamba-mini-1.7); tool calling per docs.ai21.com

nvidia_nim/meta/llama-3.3-70b-instruct.source: build.nvidia.com model card meta/llama-3.3-70b-instruct (128K context, tool calling); $0 because the NIM API serves NVIDIA Developer Program credits, not per-token billing (ProviderSpec nvidia free_info); LiteLLM's only nvidia_nim/ rows are rerankers

nvidia_nim/meta/llama-3.1-8b-instruct.source: build.nvidia.com model card meta/llama-3.1-8b-instruct (128K context, tool calling); $0 because the NIM API serves NVIDIA Developer Program credits (see nvidia_nim/meta/llama-3.3-70b-instruct)

openrouter/openai/gpt-oss-120b.source: litellm 1.99.0 bundled model_cost row openrouter/openai/gpt-oss-120b, verbatim; the row is absent from 1.106.6's bundled map and the live map (2026-10-31), so this payload prices it until LiteLLM carries it again

openrouter/openai/gpt-oss-20b.source: litellm 1.99.0 bundled model_cost row openrouter/openai/gpt-oss-20b, verbatim (see openrouter/openai/gpt-oss-120b)
